## Common Pitfalls

- Don't truncate inputs when passing files or content to the API. If the content is too long to fit in the context window, notify the user and discuss options (chunking, summarization, etc.) rather than silently truncating.
- **Prefill removed (Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Assistant message prefills (last-assistant-turn prefills) return a 400 error on Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6. Use structured outputs (`output_config.format`) or system prompt instructions to control response format instead. (One exception: the fallback-credit prefill claim - when redeeming a credit with `fallback_has_prefill_claim: true`, the server accepts the echoed assistant message; see the migration guide's refusal section.)
- **Confirm migration scope before editing:** When a user asks to migrate code to a newer Claude model without naming a specific file, directory, or file list, **ask which scope to apply first** - the entire working directory, a specific subdirectory, or a specific set of files. Do not start editing until the user confirms. Imperative phrasings like "migrate my codebase", "move my project to X", "upgrade to Sonnet 4.6", or bare "migrate to Opus 4.8" are **still ambiguous** - they tell you what to do but not where, so ask. Proceed without asking only when the prompt names an exact file, a specific directory, or an explicit file list ("migrate `app.py`", "migrate everything under `services/`", "update `a.py` and `b.py`"). See `shared/model-migration.md` Step 0.
- **`max_tokens` defaults:** Don't lowball `max_tokens` - hitting the cap truncates output mid-thought and requires a retry. For non-streaming requests, default to `~16000` (keeps responses under SDK HTTP timeouts). For streaming requests, default to `~64000` (timeouts aren't a concern, so give the model room). Only go lower when you have a hard reason: classification (`~256`), cost caps, deliberately short outputs, or **`max_tokens: 0`** for cache pre-warming (see `shared/prompt-caching.md` -> Pre-warming).
- **Disabling thinking on Claude Opus 5 has two failure modes - prefer low/medium effort instead.** (On Claude Opus 5.5, `{type: "disabled"}` is a 400 at every effort level - use `low` effort. On Claude Sonnet 5.5 it is also a 400 - try `low` effort first, and if a route must stay thinking-off, send `{type: "between_tools"}` at `high` effort or below.) Watch for a disabled-thinking setting carried forward from Opus 4.8. With it, the model occasionally writes a tool call into its **visible text** instead of a `tool_use` block (the call never runs, no error is raised), and can leak `<thinking>` tags. Turning thinking on and lowering `effort` fixes both. If a route must stay thinking-off: **delete** any don't-think/don't-reason rule, don't name thinking tags, and add *"When you use a tool, you may say a brief sentence first. If no tool can express what the user asked for, say so instead of guessing. Do not include internal or system XML tags in your response."* Details: `shared/model-migration.md` -> Two failure modes when thinking is disabled.
- **128K output tokens:** Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, and Claude Haiku 5.5 support up to 128K `max_tokens`, but the SDKs require streaming for values that large to avoid HTTP timeouts. Use `.stream()` with `.get_final_message()` / `.finalMessage()`.
- **Forced tool use removed (Claude Fable 5.1 / Claude Mythos 5.1 / Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Sonnet 5.5):** `tool_choice: {type: "any"}` and `{type: "tool", name: ...}` return a 400 (`tool_choice: type "tool" and "any" are not supported for this model.`), on `count_tokens` and Batches too. Use `{type: "auto"}` plus an explicit instruction naming the tool, `strict: true` on the tool to keep schema-valid arguments, or structured outputs (`output_config.format`) when the forced call only existed to get JSON back. `{type: "none"}` is unaffected; `disable_parallel_tool_use` still works with `auto` (at most one call).
- **Tool call JSON parsing (Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, and the 4.6/4.7/4.8 family):** Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1, Opus 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.8, and Sonnet 4.6 may produce different JSON string escaping in tool call `input` fields (e.g., Unicode or forward-slash escaping). Always parse tool inputs with `json.loads()` / `JSON.parse()` - never do raw string matching on the serialized input.
- **Structured outputs (all models):** Use `output_config: {format: {...}}` instead of the deprecated `output_format` parameter on `messages.create()`. This is a general API change, not 4.6-specific.
- **Don't reimplement SDK functionality:** The SDK provides high-level helpers - use them instead of building from scratch. Specifically: use `stream.finalMessage()` instead of wrapping `.on()` events in `new Promise()`; use typed exception classes (`Anthropic.RateLimitError`, etc.) instead of string-matching error messages; use SDK types (`Anthropic.MessageParam`, `Anthropic.Tool`, `Anthropic.Message`, etc.) instead of redefining equivalent interfaces.
- **Error handling - catch a chain, not one broad class.** A single `except APIStatusError` / `catch (AnthropicServiceException)` / `rescue APIError` loses the distinction between retryable (429, >=500, network) and non-retryable (400/404) failures. Write a most-specific-first chain - e.g. `NotFoundError` -> `RateLimitError` -> `APIStatusError` -> `APIConnectionError` (or the Go equivalent: `errors.As` into `*anthropic.Error` then `switch apierr.StatusCode { case 404: ...; case 429: ...; default: ... }`). Per-language class names and namespaces are in `shared/error-codes.md`.
- **Don't research SDK types - write first.** If a type name isn't shown in the documentation included in this skill, write the code file from the namespace/package tables in the language-specific doc and let the compiler's error point you to the right name. Do not spend turns on WebFetch, SDK-repo clones, or compiling-and-running a separate reflection program to discover type names before writing - produce the source file first, then fix what the compiler reports. A quick `strings` / `jar tf` / `javap` against the installed SDK is acceptable for locating names (it returns in seconds), but don't escalate beyond that. A file with a wrong type name is recoverable; a session spent on discovery with no file written is not.
- **Bash and text editor tools are Anthropic-defined, schema-less.** Declare `{"type": "bash_20250124", "name": "bash"}` / `{"type": "text_editor_20250728", "name": "str_replace_based_edit_tool"}` - no `input_schema`. A custom tool with your own schema named `"bash"` is a different tool. Handler paths and security checks are in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Client-Side Tools.
- **Advisor tool model pairing.** The advisor tool's `model` must be at least as capable as the request's top-level `model` - e.g. executor `claude-sonnet-5-5` -> advisor `claude-opus-5-5`. An invalid pair returns 400; a `claude-sonnet-5-5` executor accepts only the advisors its row in the pairing table lists (not Claude Opus 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6, Claude Sonnet 5, or Sonnet 4.6). Pairing table (and which advisors return plaintext vs encrypted `advisor_redacted_result` advice) in `shared/tool-use-concepts.md` § Advisor. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Agent Skills != Managed Agents.** To have Claude generate a `.pptx`/`.xlsx`/etc. via Agent Skills, call `client.beta.messages.create` with `container={"skills": [...]}`, the `code_execution_20260521` tool, and the `code-execution-2025-08-25` beta (Skills is out of beta - no `skills-2025-10-02` header needed). Do not use `client.beta.agents` / `sessions` / `environments` here - those are the Managed Agents surface, not Agent Skills.
- **MCP connector needs both halves.** `mcp_servers=[{type:"url", url, name}]` alone is rejected as a validation error - also add `tools=[{type:"mcp_toolset", mcp_server_name:<same name>}]` with beta `mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **`inference_geo` is a direct top-level request parameter** - `client.messages.create(..., inference_geo="us")` / `.inferenceGeo("us")`. Do not put it in `extra_body` / `putAdditionalBodyProperty`. (Messages API only - on Managed Agents, `inference_geo` instead nests inside the agent's `model` object, never top-level; see `shared/managed-agents-core.md` § Pinning inference geography.) Supported on Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 and later; availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`. `response.usage.inference_geo` reports where inference ran.
- **Fine-grained tool streaming is not a beta feature; this skill's default is to turn it on for streaming + client tools (the API itself still defaults to buffered).** Set `eager_input_streaming: true` on the tool definition and call the regular `client.messages.stream(...)`. There is no beta header and no `client.beta.*` path. Do not also send the legacy `fine-grained-tool-streaming-2025-05-14` beta header. Python's `@beta_tool(eager_input_streaming=True)` accepts it directly; TypeScript's `betaZodTool()` does not, so spread it on: `{ ...betaZodTool({...}), eager_input_streaming: true }`. With the field on, the API no longer coerces or validates the input, so the accumulated `partial_json` may be incomplete (`max_tokens`) or invalid - guard the parse (`shared/tool-use-concepts.md` -> Eager input streaming).
- **Cache diagnostics is beta.** Use `client.beta.messages.*` with beta `cache-diagnosis-2026-04-07`. Pass `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: null}` on the first turn and `diagnostics: {previous_message_id: <previous response id>}` on subsequent turns; the result is on `response.diagnostics`. Availability: `shared/platform-availability.md`.
- **Memory tool type is `memory_20250818`.** Declare `{"type": "memory_20250818", "name": "memory"}`. Go uses the beta-namespace type `{OfMemoryTool20250818: &anthropic.BetaMemoryTool20250818Param{}}` on `client.Beta.Messages.New`; Python/TypeScript/Ruby/PHP/C# use the non-beta `client.messages.create`; Java has both a non-beta `MemoryTool20250818` and a beta tool-runner path. Python/TypeScript provide `BetaAbstractMemoryTool` / `betaMemoryTool` helpers for implementing the backend.
- **Use a model the feature actually supports.** Some features are restricted to specific model tiers - fast mode is Claude Opus 5 / Claude Opus 5.5 / Opus 4.8 only (and Claude API only), task budgets (Messages API only - Managed Agents session budgets have no model-tier restriction) are Claude Opus 5 / Claude Opus 5.5 / Fable 5 / Claude Fable 5.1 (confirm at launch) / Claude Sonnet 5.5 / Claude Haiku 5.5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 only (not Claude Sonnet 5), and the advisor tool requires a valid executor<->advisor pair. If the user's prompt names a model that the feature doesn't support, use a supported model instead and note the substitution in the output.
- **Don't define custom types for SDK data structures:** The SDK exports types for all API objects. Use `Anthropic.MessageParam` for messages, `Anthropic.Tool` for tool definitions, `Anthropic.ToolUseBlock` / `Anthropic.ToolResultBlockParam` for tool results, `Anthropic.Message` for responses. Defining your own `interface ChatMessage { role: string; content: unknown }` duplicates what the SDK already provides and loses type safety.
- **Report and document output:** For tasks that produce reports, documents, or visualizations, the code execution sandbox has `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `matplotlib`, `pillow`, and `pypdf` pre-installed. Claude can generate formatted files (DOCX, PDF, charts) and return them via the Files API - consider this for "report" or "document" type requests instead of plain stdout text.
- **Server-tool errors don't raise.** Web search and web fetch errors return HTTP 200 with a `web_search_tool_result` / `web_fetch_tool_result` block whose `content` is a single error object (e.g. `{error_code: "max_uses_exceeded"}`) - not a raised exception. For web search, a success `content` is a *list*; an error `content` is an *object* - branch on that before indexing.
- **Managed Agents web tools ignore the environment's `networking`.** `web_search` / `web_fetch` run on Anthropic's servers in cloud *and* self-hosted environments, and Console org-level web settings apply to the Messages API only. Turn both off (`enabled: false`) unless the job needs the web; when it does and the sites are known in advance, restrict them per tool with `allowed_domains` **or** `blocked_domains` (never both; 1-64 plain hostnames per list, subdomains covered; IPs, bare TLDs, single-label and `localhost`-style names rejected on both tools; a path suffix is allowed only on `web_search`) on the toolset `configs` entry - `shared/managed-agents-tools.md` § Web search & web fetch settings.
- **Eval / hillclimb work has dedicated guides:** If the user says "hillclimb", "improve my eval score", "iterate on my prompt against an eval", or "build me an eval" - load `shared/evals/eval-hillclimb.md` or `shared/evals/build-eval.md` rather than improvising. The bundled HTML report builder is `shared/evals/report/build-report.mjs` when it is on disk (EAP install), else `shared/evals/report/build-report-lite.mjs` (always extracted with this skill); don't write a parallel one.
- **Code execution output block type:** `code_execution_20260521` returns `bash_code_execution_tool_result` (with `.content.stdout`), **not** the legacy bare `code_execution_tool_result`. Iterate `response.content` and match on the correct type.
- **Tool search: never defer everything.** The search tool itself must not have `defer_loading: true`, and at least one tool in `tools` must be non-deferred, or the API returns 400 `All tools have defer_loading set`.

## Client Initialization

```python
import anthropic

# Default - resolves credentials from the environment:
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, or ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, or an `ant auth login` profile.
# Prefer this for local dev; don't hardcode a key.
client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# Explicit API key (only when you must inject a specific key)
client = anthropic.Anthropic(api_key="your-api-key")

# Async client
async_client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic()
```

---

## Client Configuration

### Per-request overrides

Use `with_options()` to override client settings for a single call without mutating the client:

```python
client.with_options(timeout=5.0, max_retries=5).messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
```

### Timeouts

Default request timeout is 10 minutes. Pass a float (seconds) or an `anthropic.Timeout` for granular control. On timeout the SDK raises `anthropic.APITimeoutError` (and retries per `max_retries`).

```python
client = anthropic.Anthropic(timeout=20.0)
client = anthropic.Anthropic(
    timeout=anthropic.Timeout(60.0, read=5.0, write=10.0, connect=2.0),
)
```

`anthropic` 1.x is built on [`httpx2`](https://pypi.org/project/httpx2/), not `httpx`. `anthropic.Timeout` is `httpx2.Timeout`; if you import the HTTP library yourself, write `import httpx2 as httpx` - an object from the `httpx` package (`httpx.Timeout`, `httpx.Client`, transports, limits) is rejected or fails at request time. Existing `httpx`-era code is covered by the [v1 migration guide](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python/blob/main/MIGRATION.md) and `/claude-api upgrade python`.

### Retries

The SDK auto-retries connection errors, 408, 409, 429, and >=500 with exponential backoff (default 2 retries). Set `max_retries` on the client or via `with_options()`; `max_retries=0` disables.

### Async performance (aiohttp backend)

For high-concurrency async workloads, install `anthropic[aiohttp]` and pass `DefaultAioHttpClient` instead of the default httpx2 backend:

```python
from anthropic import AsyncAnthropic, DefaultAioHttpClient

async with AsyncAnthropic(http_client=DefaultAioHttpClient()) as client:
    ...
```

### Custom HTTP client (proxy, base URL)

Use `DefaultHttpxClient` / `DefaultAsyncHttpxClient` - not a raw `httpx2.Client` (and never a client from the `httpx` package) - so the SDK's default timeouts and connection limits are preserved:

```python
from anthropic import Anthropic, DefaultHttpxClient

client = Anthropic(
    base_url="http://my.test.server.example.com:8083",  # or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL env var
    http_client=DefaultHttpxClient(proxy="http://my.test.proxy.example.com"),
)
```

### Logging

Set `ANTHROPIC_LOG=debug` (or `info`) to enable SDK logging via the standard `logging` module.

```python
response = client.messages.create(
```

## System Prompts

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system="You are a helpful coding assistant. Always provide examples in Python.",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "How do I read a JSON file?"}]
)
```

### Mid-conversation system messages (model-gated)

For operator instructions that arrive mid-conversation (mode switches, injected state), append `{"role": "system", ...}` to `messages` instead of editing top-level `system` - this preserves the cached prefix and carries operator authority. Must follow a user message (or an `assistant` message ending in server-tool use), and must be either the last entry in `messages` or be followed by an `assistant` turn; cannot be `messages[0]`. Unsupported models return a 400 (`role 'system' is not supported on this model`). See `shared/prompt-caching.md` for when to use this vs. top-level `system`.

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model=MODEL_ID,  # must support mid-conversation system messages
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{"type": "text", "text": STABLE_SYSTEM, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}}],
    messages=history + [
        {"role": "user", "content": user_message},
        {"role": "system", "content": "Terse mode enabled - keep responses under 40 words."},
    ],
)  # No beta header needed - use regular client.messages.create
```

## Prompt Caching

Cache large context to reduce costs (up to 90% savings). **Caching is a prefix match** - any byte change anywhere in the prefix invalidates everything after it. For placement patterns, architectural guidance (frozen system prompt, deterministic tool order, where to put volatile content), and the silent-invalidator audit checklist, read `shared/prompt-caching.md`.

### Automatic Caching (Recommended)

Use top-level `cache_control` to automatically cache the last cacheable block in the request - no need to annotate individual content blocks:

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"},  # auto-caches the last cacheable block
    system="You are an expert on this large document...",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)
```

### Manual Cache Control

For fine-grained control, add `cache_control` to specific content blocks:

```python
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "You are an expert on this large document...",
        "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}  # default TTL is 5 minutes
    }],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)

# With explicit TTL (time-to-live)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    system=[{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "You are an expert on this large document...",
        "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "1h"}  # 1 hour TTL
    }],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)
```

### Verifying Cache Hits

```python
print(response.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens)  # tokens written to cache (~1.25x cost)
print(response.usage.cache_read_input_tokens)      # tokens served from cache (~0.1x cost)
print(response.usage.input_tokens)                 # uncached tokens (full cost)
```

If `cache_read_input_tokens` is zero across repeated identical-prefix requests, a silent invalidator is at work - `datetime.now()` or a UUID in the system prompt, unsorted `json.dumps()`, or a varying tool set. See `shared/prompt-caching.md` for the full audit table.

## Extended Thinking

> **Fable 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6:** Use adaptive thinking. `budget_tokens` is removed on Fable 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, and 4.7 (400 if sent); deprecated on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6.
> **Claude Opus 5.5:** thinking is always on - omit `thinking` (or send `{"type": "adaptive"}`, which is equivalent); `{"type": "disabled"}` returns a 400 at every effort, as does a thinking budget. Control depth with `output_config.effort` instead - the default is `medium` on this model, where Claude Opus 5 defaults to `high`.
> **Claude Opus 5:** thinking is on by default - omitting `thinking` runs adaptive (`{"type": "adaptive"}` is equivalent), unlike Opus 4.8/4.7 where omitting it meant no thinking. `{"type": "disabled"}` is accepted only at effort `high` or lower; pairing it with `xhigh`/`max` returns a 400.
> **Claude Haiku 5.5:** adaptive thinking only, on by default; `budget_tokens` returns a 400.
> **Older models:** Use `thinking: {type: "enabled", budget_tokens: N}` (must be < `max_tokens`, min 1024).

```python
# Fable 5 / Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude Opus 5 / Opus 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6: adaptive thinking (recommended)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    thinking={"type": "adaptive", "display": "summarized"},  # display opt-in: default is omitted (empty thinking text) on Fable 5/5.1, Mythos 5/5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8/4.7, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Sonnet 5
    output_config={"effort": "high"},  # low | medium | high | xhigh | max
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Solve this step by step..."}]
)

# Access thinking and response
for block in response.content:
    if block.type == "thinking":
        print(f"Thinking: {block.thinking}")
    elif block.type == "text":
        print(f"Response: {block.text}")
```

---

## Error Handling

```python
import anthropic

try:
    response = client.messages.create(...)
except anthropic.BadRequestError as e:
    print(f"Bad request: {e.message}")
except anthropic.AuthenticationError:
    print("Invalid API key")
except anthropic.PermissionDeniedError:
    print("API key lacks required permissions")
except anthropic.NotFoundError:
    print("Invalid model or endpoint")
except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
    retry_after = int(e.response.headers.get("retry-after", "60"))
    print(f"Rate limited. Retry after {retry_after}s.")
except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
    if e.status_code >= 500:
        print(f"Server error ({e.status_code}). Retry later.")
    else:
        print(f"API error: {e.message}")
except anthropic.APIConnectionError:
    print("Network error. Check internet connection.")
```

---

## Response Helpers

Every response object exposes `_request_id` (populated from the `request-id` header) - log it when reporting failures to Anthropic. Despite the underscore prefix, this property is public.

```python
message = client.messages.create(...)
print(message._request_id)       # req_018EeWyXxfu5pfWkrYcMdjWG
print(message.to_json())          # serialize the Pydantic model
print(message.to_dict())          # plain dict
```

To access raw headers or other response metadata, use `.with_raw_response`:

```python
raw = client.messages.with_raw_response.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(raw.headers.get("request-id"))
message = raw.parse()  # the Message object messages.create() would have returned
```

---

## Multi-Turn Conversations

The API is stateless - send the full conversation history each time.

```python
class ConversationManager:
    """Manage multi-turn conversations with the Claude API."""

    def __init__(self, client: anthropic.Anthropic, model: str, system: str = None):
        self.client = client
        self.model = model
        self.system = system
        self.messages = []

    def send(self, user_message: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        """Send a message and get a response."""
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})

        response = self.client.messages.create(
            model=self.model,
            max_tokens=kwargs.get("max_tokens", 16000),
            system=self.system,
            messages=self.messages,
            **kwargs
        )

        assistant_message = next(
            (b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), ""
        )
        self.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": assistant_message})

        return assistant_message

# Usage
conversation = ConversationManager(
    client=anthropic.Anthropic(),
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    system="You are a helpful assistant."
)

response1 = conversation.send("My name is Alice.")
response2 = conversation.send("What's my name?")  # Claude remembers "Alice"
```

**Rules:**

- Consecutive same-role messages are allowed - the API combines them into a single turn
- First message must be `user`
- `role: "system"` messages are allowed mid-conversation on supporting models (no beta header needed) - see § Mid-conversation system messages above

---

### Compaction (long conversations)

> **Beta, Fable 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Opus 4.8, Opus 4.7, Opus 4.6, and Sonnet 4.6.** When conversations approach the 200K context window, compaction automatically summarizes earlier context server-side. The API returns a `compaction` block; you must pass it back on subsequent requests - append `response.content`, not just the text.

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()
messages = []

def chat(user_message: str) -> str:
    messages.append({"role": "user", "content": user_message})

    response = client.beta.messages.create(
        betas=["compact-2026-01-12"],
        model="claude-opus-5-5",
        max_tokens=16000,
        messages=messages,
        context_management={
            "edits": [{"type": "compact_20260112"}]
        }
    )

    # Append full content - compaction blocks must be preserved
    messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": response.content})

    return next(block.text for block in response.content if block.type == "text")

# Compaction triggers automatically when context grows large
print(chat("Help me build a Python web scraper"))
print(chat("Add support for JavaScript-rendered pages"))
print(chat("Now add rate limiting and error handling"))
```

---

## Stop Reasons

The `stop_reason` field in the response indicates why the model stopped generating:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `end_turn` | Claude finished its response naturally |
| `max_tokens` | Hit the `max_tokens` limit - increase it or use streaming |
| `stop_sequence` | Hit a custom stop sequence |
| `tool_use` | Claude wants to call a tool - execute it and continue |
| `pause_turn` | Model paused and can be resumed (agentic flows) |
| `refusal` | Claude refused for safety reasons - check `stop_details` |

### Structured Stop Details

When `stop_reason` is `"refusal"`, the response includes a `stop_details` object with structured information about the refusal:

```python
if response.stop_reason == "refusal" and response.stop_details:
    print(f"Category: {response.stop_details.category}")   # e.g. "cyber", "bio", "reasoning_extraction", "frontier_llm", or None - see docs for the full set
    print(f"Explanation: {response.stop_details.explanation}")
```

### Refusal Fallbacks (Claude Fable 5.1) - opt in by default

Fallbacks are **opt-in**: without them a refused request simply stops. Include the server-side `fallbacks` parameter in `claude-fable-5-1` code by default - on a policy decline the API re-runs the same request on the fallback model inside the same call. A mid-stream decline is billed at normal rates, and the rescue bills at the fallback model's own rates, with cache repricing applied automatically; for a decline before any output, see [How refusals are billed](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback#how-refusals-are-billed).

```python
response = client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-fable-5-1",
    max_tokens=16000,
    betas=["server-side-fallback-2026-06-01"],
    fallbacks=[{"model": "claude-opus-4-8"}],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "..."}],
)

# Switch points: one fallback block per model that ran and declined this turn
for block in response.content:
    if block.type == "fallback":
        print(f"{block.from_.model} declined; {block.to.model} continued")

# Served-by signal - covers sticky turns, which carry no fallback block.
# Pair with stop_reason: the fallback model can itself refuse.
fallback_ran = any(
    entry.type == "fallback_message" for entry in response.usage.iterations or []
)
if fallback_ran and response.stop_reason != "refusal":
    print(f"Served by {response.model}")
```

A `stop_reason: "refusal"` on the final response means the whole chain refused. The header must be exactly `server-side-fallback-2026-06-01` **for this array form**; the newer `fallbacks: "default"` scalar form uses `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` instead (see `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Opus 5 -> New API features), and pairing either header with the other form returns a 400. The parameter is rejected on the Batches API and unavailable on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry - register the client-side `BetaRefusalFallbackMiddleware` on the client there instead. Full semantics (sticky routing, billing, streaming, echoing fallback turns back): `shared/model-migration.md` -> Migrating to Claude Fable 5.1 -> `refusal` stop reason.

---

## Cost Optimization Strategies

### 1. Use Prompt Caching for Repeated Context

```python
# Automatic caching (simplest - caches the last cacheable block)
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=16000,
    cache_control={"type": "ephemeral"},
    system=large_document_text,  # e.g., 50KB of context
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key points"}]
)

# First request: full cost
# Subsequent requests: ~90% cheaper for cached portion
```

### 2. Choose the Right Model

```python
# Default to Opus for most tasks
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",  # $4.00/$20.00 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain quantum computing"}]
)

# Use Sonnet for high-volume production workloads
standard_response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-5-5",  # $2.00/$10.00 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=16000,
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this document"}]
)

# Use Haiku only for simple, speed-critical tasks
simple_response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-haiku-5-5",  # $0.10/$0.50 per 1M tokens
    max_tokens=1024,
    output_config={"effort": "low"},
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Classify this as positive or negative"}]
)
```

### 3. Use Token Counting Before Requests

```python
count_response = client.messages.count_tokens(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    messages=messages,
    system=system
)

estimated_input_cost = count_response.input_tokens * 0.000004  # $4/1M tokens
print(f"Estimated input cost: ${estimated_input_cost:.4f}")
```

---

## Retry with Exponential Backoff

> **Note:** The Anthropic SDK automatically retries rate limit (429) and server errors (5xx) with exponential backoff. You can configure this with `max_retries` (default: 2). Only implement custom retry logic if you need behavior beyond what the SDK provides.

```python
import time
import random
import anthropic

def call_with_retry(
    client: anthropic.Anthropic,
    max_retries: int = 5,
    base_delay: float = 1.0,
    max_delay: float = 60.0,
    **kwargs
):
    """Call the API with exponential backoff retry."""
    last_exception = None

    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            return client.messages.create(**kwargs)
        except anthropic.RateLimitError as e:
            last_exception = e
        except anthropic.APIStatusError as e:
            if e.status_code >= 500:
                last_exception = e
            else:
                raise  # Client errors (4xx except 429) should not be retried

        delay = min(base_delay * (2 ** attempt) + random.uniform(0, 1), max_delay)
        print(f"Retry {attempt + 1}/{max_retries} after {delay:.1f}s")
        time.sleep(delay)

    raise last_exception
```

# SPEC schema

The builder turns a bank brief (clean specification or raw bank material: mails, policy extracts,
memos that change earlier rules, code lists) into ONE JSON object with exactly these keys.
Code turns the SPEC into a phone-agent workflow, so every value must be exact.

General rules
- Take every value from the brief and the tool API file. Never invent a rule or a value.
- When a later memo or note changes a rule, use the changed rule only.
- Sentences in `lines` are spoken word for word by the phone agent. Write them in the call language,
  short, polite, and containing exactly what the brief requires to be said. `{name}` inserts a call variable.
- Tool parameter names, enum values, response field names: copy them exactly from the tool API file.

```jsonc
{
  "bank_name": "Example Bank",
  "language": "English",
  "currency_word": "",                 // spoken after amounts, "" if the brief names no currency
  "call_variables": ["customer_id", "first_name", "last_name", "title", "now"],   // variables every call starts with

  "lines": {
    "opening": "...",                  // first sentence (who calls, recorded, ...). Must not reveal the reason before verification
    "confirm_identity": "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?",
    "ai_answer": "...",                // answer when asked "are you a robot"
    "scam_answer": "...",              // answer when asked "is this a scam"
    "identity_intro": "...",           // said right before the first security question, after the person confirmed
    "identity_failed": "...",          // said when the identity check failed (e.g. go to app/branch)
    "identity_decline_explanation": "...",
    "debt_intro": "...",               // after verification, single product: who is calling and why
    "debt_intro_multi": "...",         // same for several products
    "first_ask": "...",                // first question after stating the debt (single product)
    "first_ask_multi": "...",          // same for several products
    "confirm_question": "Do you confirm?",
    "promise_recorded": "...",         // said only after the promise tool succeeded
    "sms_sentence": "...",             // any sentence the brief requires after a recorded promise, "" if none
    "service_error": "...",            // the promise could not be recorded
    "already_paid": "...",             // what to say when the customer says they already paid
    "change_promise": "...",
    "condolence": "...",               // when the customer has died
    "no_info": "...",
    "goodbye": "..."                   // closing thanks + goodbye
  },
  "forbidden_before_verification": ["..."],   // words/topics never said before identity is verified

  "contact": { "max_asks": 2, "confirmations": ["..."], "not_confirmations": ["..."] },

  "callback": {                        // when someone else answers
    "enabled": true,
    "days": "today_or_next_business_day",   // one of: today_only, next_business_day, today_or_next_business_day
    "window_start": "HH:MM", "window_end": "HH:MM",    // inclusive
    "must_be_after_now": true,
    "max_asks": 2
  },

  "identity": {
    "field_param": "field",            // verify tool parameter that names the question
    "answer_param": "answer",          // verify tool parameter with the answer
    "questions": [                     // in the order the brief requires
      {"field": "<enum value from the tool API>", "ask": "<question to say>", "answer_format": "date|digits|year|text", "digits": 4, "spoken_name": "..."}
    ],
    "max_wrong_total": 3,
    "numeric_date_order": "DMY",       // how to read a date given only as numbers: DMY or MDY
    "response": {"answer_ok": "<bool field: this answer correct>", "all_ok": "<bool field: all passed>", "remaining": "<int field: wrong answers left>", "hint": "<hint field>", "ok": "ok"},
    "hints": [{"value": "<hint value>", "instruction": "<what the agent says/does>"}],
    "decline_max": 2
  },

  "account": {"products_field": "products", "id_field": "product_id", "type_field": "type", "past_due_field": "past_due", "days_late_field": "days_late"},

  "product_types": {                   // one entry per product type value in the tool API
    "<type value>": {"spoken": "credit card ending {card_last4}", "floor_field": "<field holding the lowest acceptable amount>", "floor_name": "minimum payment"}
  },                                   // {field} in "spoken" inserts a field of the product record

  "calendar": {"business_weekdays": [1,2,3,4,5], "holidays": ["YYYY-MM-DD"]},   // ISO weekday numbers, Monday = 1

  "bands": [                           // how late -> deadline and number of persuasion attempts
    {"name": "...", "min_days_late": 1, "max_days_late": 10,
     "deadline": {"type": "business_days_after_today", "n": 5},
     "attempts": 1}
  ],
  // deadline types: business_days_after_today (the n-th business day after today),
  //   business_days_after_today_counting_today, calendar_days_after_today (rolled back to a business day),
  //   end_of_month, end_of_next_month, fixed_date (with "date")

  "attempts": [                        // persuasion attempts in order; a band uses the first `attempts` of them
    {"number": 1, "amount": "full|floor|full_or_floor_if_full_refused", "date": "<date rule>"}
  ],
  // date rules: last_business_day_this_week_or_next_if_today, last_business_day_this_week,
  //   next_business_day, today, deadline, business_days_after_today:<n>

  "promise_tool": {"product_param": "product_id", "amount_param": "amount", "date_param": "date", "ok_field": "ok"},
  "multi_product": false,              // true when a customer can have several products
  "notes": {"enabled": false, "tool": "add_note", "product_param": "product_id", "reason_param": "reason", "reasons": ["..."]},
  "transfer": {"queue_param": "queue", "queue_to_reason": {"<queue>": "<close reason used after this transfer>"}},
  "close": {"outcome_param": "outcome", "reason_param": "reason", "no_reason_outcomes": ["..."]},

  "outcomes": [                        // EVERY row of the brief's outcome table
    {"outcome": "<value>", "reason": "<value or empty>", "when": "<when, in a few words>",
     "stage": "contact|third_party|identity|negotiate|any"}
  ],
  // stage: where in the call the outcome is decided. contact = before we know who is on the line
  //   (wrong number, unclear, deceased); third_party = someone else answered (callback...);
  //   identity = security questions; negotiate = after the debt was stated; any = can happen anywhere.

  "rules_text": {                      // the brief's rules for each step, as short imperative bullet lines ("- ...")
    "global": "...",                   // rules for the whole call (honesty, no invented terms, robot/scam questions, human requests)
    "contact": "...",                  // who is on the line
    "third_party": "...",              // someone else answered
    "identity": "...",                 // security questions
    "negotiate": "..."                 // stating the debt, dates, amounts, persuasion, special cases, confirmation, recording, multi-product rules
  }
}
```

`rules_text` must contain EVERY rule of the brief that applies in that step, including the numbers
(limits, windows, counts). It is the agent's only source for rules that the other fields do not cover.
Refer to tools by their names in the tool API file, and to call endings as "end as <reason>"
(or "end as <outcome>" when there is no reason).

"""Brief(s) + tool API -> SPEC, with Claude. Two passes: extract, then a coverage review that fixes the SPEC."""
import json, os, pathlib, re

import anthropic

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MODEL = os.environ.get("BUILDER_MODEL", "claude-opus-5-5")

SYSTEM = (
    "You convert a bank's collections brief into a machine-readable SPEC for a phone-agent generator. "
    "Precision matters more than anything: every number, date, limit, enum value and required sentence must match the brief exactly. "
    "Read raw material carefully: when a memo, mail or later note changes a rule, only the changed rule counts. "
    "Answer with a single JSON object in a ```json block and nothing else."
)


def _client():
    return anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=4)


def _ask(trace, purpose, prompt, effort="high"):
    with _client().messages.stream(
        model=MODEL, max_tokens=64000, system=SYSTEM,
        thinking={"type": "adaptive"}, output_config={"effort": effort},
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    ) as stream:
        msg = stream.get_final_message()
    text = "".join(b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text")
    trace.model_call(MODEL, purpose, msg.usage)
    m = re.search(r"```json\s*(.*?)```", text, re.S)
    raw = m.group(1) if m else text[text.find("{"): text.rfind("}") + 1]
    return json.loads(raw)


def extract_spec(brief_texts, openapi_text, trace):
    schema = (HERE / "spec_schema.md").read_text()
    briefs = "\n\n".join(f"<brief file=\"{name}\">\n{text}\n</brief>" for name, text in brief_texts)
    base = f"{schema}\n\n<tool_api>\n{openapi_text}\n</tool_api>\n\n{briefs}\n\n"
    if len(brief_texts) > 1:
        base += "The later briefs build on the earlier ones: every earlier rule applies unless a later one replaces it.\n\n"
    try:
        spec = _ask(trace, "extract the SPEC from the brief", base + "Write the SPEC for these briefs.")
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        spec = _ask(trace, "extract the SPEC (retry after invalid JSON)", base + "Write the SPEC for these briefs. Output valid JSON only.")
    review = (
        base + "Here is a SPEC written for these briefs:\n```json\n" + json.dumps(spec, indent=1) + "\n```\n\n"
        "Review it against the briefs line by line. Check: every rule of the brief is represented (in a field or in rules_text); "
        "every value is exact; rules changed by later material use the changed version; every outcome row is present with a correct stage; "
        "tool parameter and field names match the tool API exactly; required sentences are in `lines`. "
        "Return the corrected, complete SPEC (the whole object)."
    )
    try:
        spec = _ask(trace, "coverage review and correction of the SPEC", review)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        pass
    return spec

"""The builder. Brief files in, a phone agent on Freya out.

    python3 build.py briefs/brief-a.md [briefs/brief-b.md ...] [--openapi tools/openapi.json] [--slot NAME] [--spec SPEC.json]

Steps: brief -> SPEC (Claude) -> workflow (deterministic code) -> dry-run validation -> save + publish on Freya
-> export. Every step is written to traces/<slot>-<time>.jsonl.
"""
import argparse, json, pathlib, sys, time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
import freya
from builder import generate
from builder.trace import Trace


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("briefs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument("--openapi", default=str(ROOT / "tools/openapi.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--slot", help="Freya workflow slot (default: the last brief's file name)")
    ap.add_argument("--spec", help="use this SPEC file instead of extracting one (for testing the generator)")
    ap.add_argument("--no-save", action="store_true", help="build and validate only")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    slot = a.slot or pathlib.Path(a.briefs[-1]).stem
    out = ROOT / "out"; out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    trace = Trace(ROOT / "traces" / f"{slot}-{time.strftime('%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')}.jsonl")
    trace.event("inputs", briefs=a.briefs, openapi=a.openapi, slot=slot)
    openapi_text = pathlib.Path(a.openapi).read_text()

    if a.spec:
        spec = json.loads(pathlib.Path(a.spec).read_text())
        trace.event("spec_loaded", path=a.spec)
    else:
        from builder.extract import extract_spec
        spec = extract_spec([(pathlib.Path(b).name, pathlib.Path(b).read_text()) for b in a.briefs], openapi_text, trace)
    (out / f"{slot}.spec.json").write_text(json.dumps(spec, indent=1))
    trace.event("spec_written", path=f"out/{slot}.spec.json", outcomes=len(spec.get("outcomes") or []))

    wf = generate.build(spec, json.loads(openapi_text))
    (out / f"{slot}.workflow.json").write_text(json.dumps(wf, indent=1))
    trace.event("workflow_generated", nodes=len(wf["nodes"]), bytes=len(json.dumps(wf)))

    if not a.no_save:
        freya.validate_workflow(slot, wf)
        trace.event("dry_run_ok")
        ids = freya.save_workflow(slot, wf, state_file=str(ROOT / ".freya-agents.json"))
        trace.event("saved_on_freya", **ids)
        path = freya.export_workflow(ids["workflow_id"], str(out / f"{slot}.export.workflow.json"))
        trace.event("exported", path=path)
        print(json.dumps(ids))
    trace.close(slot=slot)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
Plan yenilendi ve iş başladı. Bundan sonrası Freya key'ine bağlı, o yüzden burada duruyorum.

## Ne yapıyoruz, kısaca
Bir **fabrika** yazıyoruz. Brief'i okuyor ve Freya'da çalışan telefon ajanını kendisi kuruyor. Ajanı elle yapmıyoruz, marka/logo yok. Çıktı bir workflow JSON'u: Freya'ya yükleniyor ve dışa aktarılıp submit ediliyor. Planın tamamı [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) içinde: zaman çizelgesi, iş bölümü ve riskler.

## Bugüne kadar yapılanlar (19:02 itibarıyla)
1. **Kit'in tamamını okudum:** iki brief, 3 doküman, openapi, 13 case, örnek ajan ve örnek builder.
2. **Ortamı kurdum:** Python 3.12 venv, git repo. Makinede `claude` CLI çalışmıyor, o yüzden builder Anthropic API'yi doğrudan çağıracak.
3. **Builder'ın çekirdeği yazıldı:**
   - [builder/generate.py](builder/generate.py): spec + openapi'den workflow'u kuruyor. Bu kısım LLM kullanmıyor, aynı girdiden hep aynı çıktıyı veriyor.
   - [builder/runtime_code.py](builder/runtime_code.py): ajanın içinde çalışan Python kodu. İş günü, tatil, deadline, floor ve deneme tarihlerini hesaplıyor. Kurala uymayan bir promise ya da callback'i bankaya gitmeden durduruyor. Her tool sonucuna ajanın bir sonraki adımda ne yapacağını ekliyor.
   - Kapanış kodu (outcome/reason) ve zorunlu cümleler (SMS cümlesi, taziye, "app'e gidin") modele bırakılmadı. Bunları kod belirliyor, sabit metin olarak okunuyor.
   - [builder/extract.py](builder/extract.py): Claude Opus 5.5 brief'i spec'e çeviriyor, ikinci bir geçişte de eksik kural var mı diye kontrol ediyor.
   - [build.py](build.py): tek komutla brief → spec → workflow → doğrulama → Freya'ya kaydetme → export → trace.
4. **Lokal test geçti.** 13 case'in hepsinde hesaplanan deadline, floor ve tarihler beklenen sonuçla aynı çıktı. Örnekler: PUB-04'te 6 Kasım reddedilip 23 Ekim öneriliyor. PUB-07'de 26 Ekim tatil olduğu için 27 Ekim öneriliyor. PUB-13'te iki ürüne ayrı deadline (30 Ekim ve 23 Ekim) çıkıyor.

Henüz **hiçbir şey Freya'da koşmadı**. Workflow formatının platformda kabul edilip edilmeyeceğini, gerçek konuşmalarda nasıl davrandığını ve skoru bilmiyoruz. Bir de üretilen workflow 211KB; platformun bunu kabul edip etmeyeceği belli değil, ilk kayıtta göreceğiz.

## Senden lazım olanlar
1. **[env.sh](env.sh) dosyasını doldur:**
   - `FREYA_API_KEY=fak_...`: staging-app'te API keys bölümünden.
   - `FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY=`: 16 karakter veya daha uzun, kendin uydurduğun bir şifre. Hep aynısını kullanacağız.
   - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...`: builder'ın kendi model çağrıları için.
2. **Boş bir GitHub repo linki.** Submit'te repo ve commit isteniyor.
3. **Solo mu, takım mı?**

Doldurunca "tamam" yazman yeter. Sırada şunlar var: baz skor (örnek ajan), bizim ajanın Brief A'daki ilk koşusu ve fail eden case'leri transcript'ten tek tek düzeltmek.

From: Ines Varga <ops-lead@nordlicht-kredit.example>
To: Vendor onboarding
Subject: FW: material for the reminder-call bot (please read the memo at the bottom, it overrides section 4)

Hi team,

as discussed, below is everything we have. Sorry it is a bit of a pile. Policy extract first, then the
outcome code list from our core system, then Jonas' memo from last week, which changes a few things.
Customers are small business owners (sole traders). All data is synthetic.

Ines

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
POLICY EXTRACT — NordLicht Kredit, Reminder Calls (version 2.3)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Greeting. The assistant introduces itself as "the automated assistant of NordLicht Kredit" and says
   the conversation is recorded for quality purposes. It then asks to speak to the account holder by
   full name ("May I speak with {first_name} {last_name}?"). No mention of arrears, money, the bank
   account or any facility before the security check is passed.

2. Wrong person. If someone else answers: do not leave any message about the reason. Ask for a good
   time to call back. Callbacks are booked for the next business day only, between 09:00 and 17:30.
   If the person cannot give a time in that window after being asked twice, close with NR-02.
   Number not known to them: NR-03. Account holder passed away: express condolences, close with NR-04.

3. Security. Two questions, in this order: the postcode of the registered business address, then the
   year the business was founded. Up to two wrong answers in total are tolerated; the third wrong
   answer ends the check (close with NV-01, refer the customer to online banking). A customer who will
   not answer after one explanation: NV-02.

4. Arrangements. (a) Business days are Monday to Friday; bank holidays: 2026-12-24, 2026-12-25,
   2026-12-31, 2027-01-01. (b) Customers 1–20 days in arrears: latest arrangement date is the
   10th business day after the call; one attempt to persuade. (c) 21–60 days: latest date is the
   5th business day after the call; two attempts. (d) The agent always asks for the full overdue
   amount first. Lowest acceptable amount: the "min_due" figure for overdrafts, the "rate" figure for
   term loans. (e) Persuasion attempt one proposes the full amount on the next business day; attempt
   two proposes the lowest acceptable amount on the latest arrangement date.

5. Disputes / already paid / hardship as usual: no arrangement. Hardship customers are offered the
   welfare team (queue "care"). Requests for restructuring go to queue "workout". A customer who asks
   for a person is transferred to queue "desk" after one offer to help.

6. Read the arrangement back and get an explicit yes before booking it. If booking fails twice, tell the
   customer and close with NP-05. After a booked arrangement say: "A confirmation letter will follow by
   post."

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
OUTCOME CODES (core banking, table OUTC)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
code   | close_call status | sub_status
ARR-01 | arrangement       | -
PD-01  | settled           | -
TR-01  | handed_over       | workout
TR-02  | handed_over       | desk
TR-03  | handed_over       | care
NP-01  | no_arrangement    | declined
NP-02  | no_arrangement    | hardship
NP-03  | no_arrangement    | contested
NP-05  | no_arrangement    | system_fault
NV-01  | unverified        | failed_check
NV-02  | unverified        | refused_check
NR-01  | not_contacted     | callback_booked
NR-02  | not_contacted     | no_time
NR-03  | not_contacted     | unknown_number
NR-04  | not_contacted     | bereavement
NR-05  | not_contacted     | unclear

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
MEMO — J. Brandt, Collections Policy, 2 October 2026
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Effective immediately, changes to the reminder-call policy:
- Section 4(c): customers 21–60 days in arrears get the 6th business day (not the 5th).
- Section 4(e): attempt one now proposes the full amount on the last business day of the current week
  (if the call is on that day, the last business day of the following week).
- Callbacks (section 2): the window ends at 18:00, not 17:30.
- 2026-12-31 is no longer a bank holiday.
Everything else stays as it is.

# Freya "Build the Builder": a builder that turns a bank brief into a phone agent

```bash
source env.sh                                   # FREYA_API_KEY, FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
python3 build.py briefs/brief-a.md briefs/brief-b.md --slot my-agent
python3 build.py <final-brief.md> --openapi <its-openapi.json> --slot final-1
```

One command, no manual step: brief(s) + tool API in → a published Freya workflow, its export
(`out/<slot>.export.workflow.json`) and a trace (`traces/<slot>-<time>.jsonl`) out.

## How it works

The phone agent runs on a fixed, small model, and a customer counts only if all three runs pass.
So the builder leaves as little reasoning as possible to that model. Dates, amounts, outcome codes and
mandatory sentences come from code. The model only holds the conversation.

```
brief(s) + openapi.json
  1. SPEC extraction (Claude Opus 5.5)            builder/extract.py, schema in builder/spec_schema.md
     - pass 1: brief -> SPEC (values, rules, sentences, outcome table with semantic roles)
     - pass 2: coverage review against the brief (memos that change rules, missing rules)
     - mechanical checks (placeholders, roles, tool enums, dates) + LLM repair
  2. Workflow generation (deterministic Python)   builder/generate.py
     - tool definitions read from the openapi file (field names, enums), nothing hard-coded
     - nodes: setup -> opening -> third_party | identity -> load_account -> compute -> negotiate -> end_* -> finalize -> goodbye
  3. Runtime code inside the workflow             builder/runtime_code.py
     - code nodes: business days, holidays, per-product band/deadline/floor, the offer sequence
       with exact sentences, a DATE LOOKUP table telling the agent what to offer for any day
     - tool pre-hooks: normalise dates/digits, block a promise or callback that breaks the rules
     - tool post-hooks: add `what_to_do_next` to every result
     - finalize: outcome + reason from what really happened (transfer, promises, notes) and the
       closing words; close_call is a lifecycle tool with baked values
  4. Save + publish on Freya (same slot = update in place), dry-run validation, one chat-turn smoke test
  5. Export + trace
```

## Tests

- `tests/test_runtime.py`: runs the workflow's code nodes and hooks locally on the 13 practice cases.
- `tests/test_fake_c.py`: the same on a made-up raw-material brief with other field names and outcome
  codes (`fixtures/fake/`), to check that nothing depends on the public briefs.
- `tools/run_cases.py`: the kit's simulator runner.

`KIT_README.md` is the organisers' kit README.

```
     - tool pre-hooks: normalise dates/digits, block a promise or callback that breaks the rules
     - tool post-hooks: add `what_to_do_next` to every result
     - finalize: outcome + reason from what really happened (transfer, promises, notes) and the
       closing words; close_call is a lifecycle tool with baked values
  4. Save + publish on Freya (same slot = update in place), dry-run validation, one chat-turn smoke test
  5. Export + trace
```

## Tests

- `tests/test_runtime.py`: runs the workflow's code nodes and hooks locally on the 13 practice cases.
- `tests/test_fake_c.py`: the same on a made-up raw-material brief with other field names and outcome
  codes (`fixtures/fake/`), to check that nothing depends on the public briefs.
- `tools/run_cases.py`: the kit's simulator runner.

`KIT_README.md` is the organisers' kit README.

# Brief D: Harbor Credit Union, member payment reminders

Harbor Credit Union is fictional. All data is synthetic.

## 1. Purpose

Harbor Credit Union calls members who are behind on up to three loans. The assistant confirms the member,
verifies identity, explains the arrears, agrees a payment where possible and closes with the right code.

## 2. Call data

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `customer_id` | Pass to every tool. |
| `first_name`, `last_name` | The member. |
| `title` | `Mr`, `Ms` or `Mx`. Address the member as title plus last name. |
| `now` | Current date and time. Use it for every date rule. |

## 3. Opening

1. Say: "Hi, this is Harbor Credit Union's virtual assistant." Then ask "Is this {title} {last_name}?". Say nothing about
   money, loans or arrears before identity is verified.
2. Accept "yes", "speaking" or the member's name. Anything else: ask once more, then close as `no_contact` / `not_confirmed`.
3. Someone else answers: ask when the member is available. Book a callback with `schedule_callback` for **today only**,
   between 12:00 and 20:00 and at least one hour after `now`. Otherwise close `no_contact` / `no_slot`. If booked: `no_contact` / `rebooked`.
4. Wrong number: `no_contact` / `wrong_person`.

## 4. Identity

5. Ask the member's postcode first, then their date of birth. Call `verify_identity` for each answer.
6. Two wrong answers in total fail the check: close as `identity` / `failed` and suggest calling the branch.
7. `verify_identity` may answer `hint: "partial_postcode"`: ask for the full postcode; this is not a wrong answer.
8. A member who refuses to answer: explain it protects them, ask once more, then `identity` / `refused`.

## 5. The arrears

9. After verification call `get_account` and say each loan in one sentence: type, amount behind, days behind.

## 6. Payment arrangement

10. Deadlines by days behind:

| days behind | latest payment date | attempts |
|---|---|---|
| 1–14 | 14 calendar days after today (if that is not a business day, the business day before) | 1 |
| 15–30 | 10 calendar days after today, same adjustment | 2 |
| 31–90 | the last business day of the current month | 3 |

11. Business days are Monday to Friday except 2026-11-26 and 2026-12-25.
12. The minimum the union accepts is the `minimum_due` of each loan. Always ask for the full amount first.
13. Attempts: 1) full amount on the next business day; 2) the minimum on the latest date; 3) the minimum on the
    next business day.
14. Read back loan, amount and date and ask "Shall I book that?". Book with `create_promise` after a yes.
    After booking say "Your reminder email is on its way."
15. Booking failed twice: say so, close as `no_deal` / `system`.

## 7. Other situations

16. Already paid: thank them, explain it may take two business days to show, close `cleared`.
17. Disputes: `no_deal` / `disputed`. Hardship (illness, job loss, bereavement): no pressure, offer the member care
    team (`transfer_to_agent`, queue `care`); declined → `no_deal` / `hardship`; accepted → `handover` / `care`.
18. Wants to talk to a person: transfer at once, queue `staff`, close `handover` / `staff`.
19. Refused after the attempts: `no_deal` / `refused`. For loans without a deal, use `add_note` with the loan and
    reason (`refused`, `hardship`, `disputed`, `cleared`, `system`).
20. Promise booked for at least one loan: `deal`.

## 8. Close

21. Say goodbye, then `close_call` with the code. Codes: `deal`, `cleared`, `handover`/`care|staff`,
    `no_deal`/`refused|hardship|disputed|system`, `identity`/`failed|refused`,
    `no_contact`/`not_confirmed|no_slot|rebooked|wrong_person`.

2. **Kontrol geçişi spec'i baştan yazmayacak**, sadece değişen alanları döndürecek. Bu, çıktının yaklaşık yarısı.

"""Brief(s) + tool API -> SPEC, with Claude. Two passes: extract, then a coverage review that fixes the SPEC."""
import json, os, pathlib, re

import anthropic

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
MODEL = os.environ.get("BUILDER_MODEL", "claude-opus-5-5")

SYSTEM = (
    "You convert a bank's collections brief into a machine-readable SPEC for a phone-agent generator. "
    "Precision matters more than anything: every number, date, limit, enum value and required sentence must match the brief exactly. "
    "Read raw material carefully: when a memo, mail or later note changes a rule, only the changed rule counts. "
    "Answer with a single JSON object in a ```json block and nothing else."
)


def _client():
    return anthropic.Anthropic(max_retries=4)


def _ask(trace, purpose, prompt, effort="high"):
    with _client().messages.stream(
        model=MODEL, max_tokens=64000, system=SYSTEM,
        thinking={"type": "adaptive"}, output_config={"effort": effort},
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
    ) as stream:
        msg = stream.get_final_message()
    text = "".join(b.text for b in msg.content if b.type == "text")
    trace.model_call(MODEL, purpose, msg.usage)
    m = re.search(r"```json\s*(.*?)```", text, re.S)
    raw = m.group(1) if m else text[text.find("{"): text.rfind("}") + 1]
    return json.loads(raw)


ROLES = {"promise", "paid", "transferred", "refused", "hardship", "dispute", "service_error", "id_failed", "id_declined",
         "callback", "no_callback", "wrong_number", "deceased", "unclear", "other"}
NEEDED_LINES = ["opening", "confirm_identity", "identity_intro", "identity_failed", "debt_intro", "first_ask", "confirm_question",
                "promise_recorded", "full_offer", "floor_offer", "goodbye"]



def extract_spec(brief_texts, openapi_text, trace):
    schema = (HERE / "spec_schema.md").read_text()
    briefs = "\n\n".join(f"<brief file=\"{name}\">\n{text}\n</brief>" for name, text in brief_texts)
    base = f"{schema}\n\n<tool_api>\n{openapi_text}\n</tool_api>\n\n{briefs}\n\n"
    if len(brief_texts) > 1:
        base += "The later briefs build on the earlier ones: every earlier rule applies unless a later one replaces it.\n\n"
    try:
        spec = _ask(trace, "extract the SPEC from the brief", base + "Write the SPEC for these briefs.")
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
        spec = _ask(trace, "extract the SPEC (retry after invalid JSON)", base + "Write the SPEC for these briefs. Output valid JSON only.")
    review = (
        base + "Here is a SPEC written for these briefs:\n```json\n" + json.dumps(spec, indent=1) + "\n```\n\n"
        "Review it against the briefs line by line. Check: every rule of the brief is represented (in a field or in rules_text); "
        "every value is exact; rules changed by later material use the changed version; every outcome row is present with a correct stage; "
        "tool parameter and field names match the tool API exactly; required sentences are in `lines`. "
        "Return the corrected, complete SPEC (the whole object)."
    )
    try:
        spec = _ask(trace, "coverage review and correction of the SPEC", review)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, anthropic.APIError) as e:
        trace.event("review_failed_keeping_first_spec", error=str(e)[:200])
    openapi = json.loads(openapi_text)
    for attempt in range(2):
        found = problems(spec, openapi)
        trace.event("spec_check", attempt=attempt, problems=found)
        if not found:
            break
        fix = (base + "Here is a SPEC written for these briefs:\n```json\n" + json.dumps(spec, indent=1) + "\n```\n\n"
               "An automatic check found these problems:\n- " + "\n- ".join(found) + "\n\nFix them and return the whole corrected SPEC.")
        try:
            spec = _ask(trace, "repair the SPEC after the automatic check", fix, effort="medium")
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError, anthropic.APIError) as e:
            trace.event("repair_failed_keeping_spec", error=str(e)[:200])
            break
    return spec

    spec = json.load(open(ROOT / "fixtures/brief-ab.llm-spec.json")); wf = generate.build(spec, json.load(open(ROOT / "tools/openapi.json")))
    v = {"customer_id": "c", "first_name": "M", "last_name": "B", "title": "Mr", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"}
    prods = [{"product_id": "p1", "type": "credit_card", "card_last4": "9015", "past_due": 510, "days_late": 16, "minimum_payment": 153},
             {"product_id": "p2", "type": "personal_loan", "past_due": 1320, "days_late": 16, "instalment_amount": 440}]
    for i, p in enumerate(prods):
        for k, x in p.items(): v[f"load_account_response.data.products.{i}.{k}"] = x
    run(node_code(wf, "compute"), v)
    nt = tool(wf, "negotiate", "add_note")
    conv1 = "AGENT: Can you pay all of them today?\nUSER: No.\nAGENT: Can you pay the full 1320 on Friday 16 October?\nUSER: No."
    cfg = {"headers": {"X-Conversation": conv1}, "body": {"customer_id": "c", "product_id": "p2", "reason": "refused"}}
    run(nt["pre_process_code"], v, config=cfg); print("one offer only ->", v["note_block"][:160], "| header removed:", "X-Conversation" not in cfg["headers"])
    assert v["note_block"] and cfg["body"]["customer_id"] == "blocked-by-agent-policy"
    conv2 = conv1 + "\nAGENT: I can record the instalment amount of 440 on Friday 23 October; the rest stays overdue.\nUSER: No."
    cfg = {"headers": {"X-Conversation": conv2}, "body": {"customer_id": "c", "product_id": "p2", "reason": "refused"}}
    v["note_checked"] = ""
    run(nt["pre_process_code"], v, config=cfg); print("both offers ->", repr(v["note_block"]))
    assert not v["note_block"] and cfg["body"]["customer_id"] == "c"
    print("NOTE CHECK OK")


test_note_check()
EOF

## Gece özeti (23:25)

**`talkative` son koşu: 9/13.** PUB-03 bu kez geçti; PUB-06 ve PUB-12 düştü. `talkative` stilinde koşudan koşuya **yüksek değişkenlik** var: aynı ajan 9–10/13 arasında gidip geliyor ve fail eden case'ler her seferinde farklı. Bunun büyük kısmı platformun konuşkan müşteriyi cümle ortasında bölmesinden kaynaklanıyor. Bu durum bütün takımları etkileyen bir simülasyon davranışı. Bizim tarafımızda kesik mesaj oranını %72'den %58'e indirdik ve `talkative` skorunu 7'den 9–10'a çıkardık.

### Bugünün sonu
| Ölçüm | Başlangıç | Şimdi |
|---|---|---|
| Varsayılan stil, 13 case × 3 (sıkı) | 6/13 | **11/13** (kalan 2 = not farkı, ajan hatası değil) |
| `talkative` | 7/13 | 9–10/13 |
| Diğer stiller (pieces, corrects, asks_back, in_words) | — | 9–10/13 (bu ayarlardan önceki ölçüm) |
| Gizli brief taklitleri (C: dağınık ham, D: farklı yapı) | — | Çökmeden, doğru spec |
| Build süresi | — | ~2,5 dk (LLM dahil) |
| Build maliyeti | ~$0,6 | ~$0,3 |

**Sağlamlık için eklenenler:** Freya API'de geçici hata olursa yeniden deneme, Anthropic API hatasında son geçerli spec'le devam, spec için otomatik kontrol + onarım, her şey GitHub'da.

### Yarın (Pazar) planı
1. **09:00–12:00:** Kimlik adımında konuşkan müşteriyi yanlışlıkla "reddetti" sayma hatası (PUB-12) için deterministik bir koruma yazmak. Diğer stilleri yeni ayarlarla yeniden ölçmek.
2. **12:00–15:00:** Sahte brief D'yi Freya'da uçtan uca kurmak (yapısal kontrol). Final runbook'u kronometreyle prova etmek.
3. **18:00:** Özellik dondurma.
4. **20:00:** Final brief'ler → builder her biri için bir kez → export → commit → submit.

    for words, prod, want, phrase in cases:

        assert ok or words.startswith("Monday the 25th")
    for amt, phrase in (("410", "acceptable"), ("100", "below"), ("600", "more than"), ("180", "acceptable")):
        r = run_tool(code, v, {"amount": amt, "product": "p1"}); print(amt, "->", r["what_to_do_next"][:120]); assert phrase in r["what_to_do_next"]

input.content:
# Ostsee Sparbank — Telephone arrears policy (excerpt, rev. 7)

All data is synthetic.

**Scope.** Automated calls to customers with overdue overdrafts or instalment loans (up to three per customer).
Language: English.

**A. Who we talk to**
A1. Open with: "Good day, this is the automated service of Ostsee Sparbank." Then ask to speak to the customer by
first and last name. Nothing about the reason for the call before the security check.
A2. If somebody else answers, do NOT arrange any call back. Thank them, say we will try again another time, and close
with code 31. Number unknown to them: code 32. Customer deceased: express condolences, code 33.
A3. If after two asks it is unclear who answered: code 34.

**B. Security**
B1. Three questions in this order: date of birth, postcode, last four digits of the phone number. Each answer is
checked with `verify_identity`.
B2. A total of two wrong answers ends the check: tell the customer to visit a branch with ID; code 41.
B3. A customer who refuses to answer: explain why once, then code 42.

**C. Arrears**
C1. After the check, call `get_account` and tell the customer each overdue product with amount and days overdue.
C2. Lowest acceptable payment for every product: 30 % of the overdue amount, but never less than 25.00.
C3. Payment dates: at most 10 calendar days from today for customers up to 30 days overdue; up to the last
business day of the current month for 31–90 days. If that day is not a business day, use the business day before.
C4. Business days: Monday to Friday, except 2026-12-24, 2026-12-25, 2026-12-31 and 2027-01-01.
C5. If the customer names a weekend or holiday, propose the business day **before** it. A date beyond the limit cannot
be accepted: say so and ask for another date within the limit.
C6. "Next Monday" etc. means the next such day to come.
C7. Ask for the full amount first. Persuasion: one attempt for up to 30 days overdue (full amount on the limit date);
two for longer (full amount on the next business day, then the lowest amount on the limit date).
C8. Confirm amount, date and product, then call `create_promise`. After success say: "We will send you a letter
confirming this arrangement." If it fails twice, apologise and close with code 25.

**D. Special cases**
D1. Already paid: say a payment can take up to two business days to show; code 22.
D2. Disputed debt: code 23. Hardship (illness, unemployment, bereavement): offer the hardship team
(`transfer_to_agent`, queue `hardship`); accepted → code 52, declined → code 24.
D3. Customer asks for a person: transfer immediately to queue `service`, code 51.
D4. Refusal after all attempts: code 21. Promise recorded for at least one product: code 10.

**E. Closing**
E1. Always thank the customer and say goodbye, then call `close_call` with `code` = the code above.

"""Brief E (numeric codes, code-only close_call, per-band offer plans, no callbacks, percent floors). No network."""
import json, sys, pathlib
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
from builder import generate
from tests.test_runtime import node_code, tool, run, run_tool

spec = json.load(open(ROOT / "fixtures/fake/brief-e.llm-spec.json")); wf = generate.build(spec, json.load(open(ROOT / "fixtures/fake/openapi-e.json")))

         {"product_id": "p2", "type": "instalment_loan", "overdue": 60, "days_overdue": 45}]

run(node_code(wf, "setup"), v); run(node_code(wf, "compute"), v)

assert P[0]["floor"] == 120 and P[1]["floor"] == 25          # 30 % of 400; 30 % of 60 = 18 -> minimum 25

assert v2["close_outcome"] == "52"
cfg = {"body": {"customer_id": "c", "code": v2["close_outcome"]}}
run(wf["tools"][0]["pre_process_code"], v2, config=cfg); print("close body", cfg["body"])
print("FAKE E OK")
EOF

- **Konuşkan müşteri ayarı:** Ajan 4 sn bekliyor; yarım kalan mesaja "I'm listening." diyor.

Son ölçümler (kalan fail'ler tek ürünlü müşteriye yazılan not farkından geliyor; bu, Brief B'nin kuralı):

| Test | Sonuç | Not farkı dışında fail |
|---|---|---|

| pieces (sürüm 28) | 11/13 | 0 |
| talkative / asks_back / corrects / in_words | 9–11/13 | 0–2 |

Title: Build the Builder | Freya × Y Combinator
URL: https://www.freyavoice.ai/hackathon
Source element: <main>
---
What this is

A bank has customers who are late on a payment. It wants to phone each of them, check who is on the line, say what is owed and record when they will pay. On Freya, software makes that call instead of a person.

Phone agent
Your credit card has 420 dollars past due. Can you pay today?

Customer
Not today. I can do it on Friday.

Phone agent
420 dollars on Friday the sixteenth. Do you confirm?

Customer
Yes.

create_promise  420.00  2026-10-16
recorded in the bank's system

A piece of one call. The last line is what the bank's system keeps. We check that record, and we check the conversation.

That software does not know the bank's rules by itself. Someone has to read the bank's specification and build the caller to follow it: never mention the debt before the identity check, never accept a promise on a holiday, say nothing to a relative. Today a person does this by hand, and one bank takes days.

The question of this hackathon: can a program do that work instead?

Three words used on this page
Phone agent
The software that talks to the customer. It lives on Freya as a workflow: steps, prompts and tools.
Brief
The bank's specification for these calls: who to ask for, how to check identity, which payment dates are allowed, how to close the call.
Builder
The program you write. It reads a brief and creates the phone agent. Nobody edits the phone agent by hand.

You write the builder. We score the phone agent it creates.

Brief
policies
tool API docs
practice customers

creates the phone agent
tests and improves it

Phone agent

conditional routes
tool calls
Our benchmark

talk to the phone agent
we read the bank's records
score = cases passed / cases run
A new brief goes in, a different phone agent comes out, no edits by hand.
One run. You write the orange box. Everything else is provided.
How the weekend goes
You download the kit from the Data tab. Two briefs, the bank's tool API, thirteen practice customers, the Freya workflow reference and a small working builder.
You run the sample builder. It creates a phone agent on Freya in your workspace.
You test that phone agent. Simulated customers talk to it in text. You see which ones it handled correctly and why the others failed.
You write your own builder and repeat steps 2 and 3 as often as you like.
On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. Same kind of call, different rules: other identity questions, other limits and deadlines, another outcome table, another calendar. The seven tool names stay the same. Their fields and allowed values can change.
You run your builder once on each new brief and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen. The share they handle correctly is your score.
Start
Sat 10:00 UTC
kit and keys
build against the 13 practice cases
Hidden briefs open
Sun 17:00 UTC
run your builder
Close
Sun 20:00 UTC
submit
Results
after review
The three hours in orange are for running the builder and fixing bugs, not for tuning it to the new briefs.
What counts
Only the phone agents are scored. Your rank comes from their score. We also rerun the builders of the top entries to verify them. Build time is the second tie-break.
A customer counts as handled when the bank's records are right afterwards and the conversation followed the brief. There is no partial credit.
The builder must work alone. One command, a brief as input, a phone agent as output. No manual edits after it runs.
The final briefs are hidden so that a builder tuned to the two public briefs does not win. It has to read a brief it has never seen.
After the hidden briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a hidden brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
Calls are in English. The phone agent gets the date and time of the call as a variable, now. Every date rule uses it.
Every phone agent runs on the same Freya model. Your builder may use any model or coding agent you like.
Inside a phone agent

A phone agent on Freya is a workflow. Each step has its own prompt and tools. Conditional routes decide which step takes the conversation next. Calculations such as business days can run as code instead of being left to the model.
